experience.title: Full Stack Robotics Engineering Internship
experience.tagline: Multidisciplinary robotics training across mechanical design, embedded control, kinematics, vision, AI, and robot interfaces
experience.summary: During a two-month robotics training internship, I worked across mechanical design, embedded control, robot kinematics, computer vision, AI, and robotic interfaces. The experience combined CAD and engineering analysis with physical robot assembly, embedded programming, and web/mobile control interfaces.
features: Designed robotic-arm concepts in SolidWorks, including a complete 5-DOF mechanical assembly with links, joint structures and motor mounts
Redesigned a robotic-arm joint bracket with an integrated bearing housing and evaluated it using SolidWorks Simulation FEA
Performed Denavit-Hartenberg forward kinematics, static payload torque calculations, and servo-motor selection for robotic-arm applications
Assembled and programmed a physical 5-DOF robotic-arm training kit using Arduino and ESP32
Built robot-control interfaces across web and mobile platforms using PHP, MySQL, Flutter, ESP32, HTTP and JSON
Worked on Python/OpenCV computer-vision exercises and AI voice-assistant applications with speech-to-text and text-to-speech integration
experience.architecture: The internship was structured as a multidisciplinary robotics training program. Mechanical CAD and analysis tasks were paired with embedded-control exercises and software interfaces, allowing each subsystem to be developed independently and then connected through robot-control workflows.
experience.results: Completed the internship with hands-on exposure across the full robotics stack, from mechanical concepts and actuator sizing to embedded control, computer vision, and operator interfaces. Project repositories and training work were documented on GitHub.

projects.title: 3-DOF SCARA Robotic Arm
projects.tagline: Independently designed, manufactured, programmed, and physically validated from CAD to autonomous cell integration.
projects.summary: A 3-DOF SCARA robotic arm independently developed from concept to physical prototype. I owned the mechanical design, DFM, dimensional tolerancing, bearing fits, BOM, manufacturing drawings, FDM production, assembly, electronics, ESP32 firmware, kinematics, browser-based control, testing, and MQTT integration.
features: Two-stage GT2 belt transmission with NEMA 17 steppers, DRV8825 drivers, bearings, limit switches, and servo gripper
DFM, dimensional tolerancing, fits and clearances, and bearing-fit principles applied through physical prototyping
ESP32 C++ firmware with homing, forward/inverse kinematics, Cartesian point control, motion limits, and programmable recipes
Engineering drawings, BOM, manufacturing-ready CAD, and PLA+ FDM production with post-processing
Three-node MQTT integration with a vision-enabled conveyor and mobile robot for autonomous box transfer and handling
projects.architecture: The ESP32 handles automatic homing, motion limits, forward and inverse kinematics, Cartesian point commands, stepper control, gripper operation, and stored motion recipes. A browser interface supports manual control, point-to-point motion, sequence creation, storage, and playback. MQTT connects the arm to a vision-enabled conveyor and mobile robot so subsystems can trigger the next stage of the automated material-handling sequence.
projects.results: Topology optimization drove a physical redesign of Arm Link 1, reducing mass by 16.5% from 201 g to 168 g while retaining critical mounting and load-bearing regions. The revised PLA+ components were manufactured and tested, the arm repeatedly handled a 100 g payload at full extension, and the integrated system demonstrated autonomous box transfer and handling.

projects.title: WD Drone: TEKNOFEST 2026
projects.tagline: Autonomous rotary-wing UAV developed from requirements and simulation through integration and flight testing.
projects.role: Founding Team Member | Autonomous Control & Simulation
projects.summary: A six-month multidisciplinary UAV R&D project for TEKNOFEST 2026. I contributed to system requirements, UAV architecture, autonomy and simulation, computer vision, flight-controller integration, technical coordination, mechanical development, and staged physical testing across a six-member team.
features: System requirements, UAV architecture, component selection, BOM/costing, and technical documentation during the R&D phase
Mechanical development support including component placement, BOM development, prototyping, assembly, fastener selection, SolidWorks structural FEA, and physical load validation
Custom Gazebo/ArduPilot SITL environment for waypoint search, visual target approach, payload delivery, and RTL
Raspberry Pi 5, Camera Module 3, and Cube Orange integrated through MAVLink over UART using pymavlink
OpenCV color and geometric target detection at approximately 30 FPS
Staged subsystem, ground, failsafe, and flight-test workflow with flight-controller configuration and debugging
projects.architecture: The Camera Module 3 feeds frames to a Raspberry Pi 5 running OpenCV. Color and geometric target detections generate target-center offsets for mission logic, while pymavlink exchanges commands and telemetry with the Cube Orange over MAVLink via UART/TELEM2. The complete search, approach, payload-release, and RTL sequence was rehearsed in Gazebo with ArduPilot SITL before transfer to the real platform.
projects.results: Five staged flight-test sessions validated autonomous waypoint flight, flight-mode transitions, real target-detection and payload-release subsystems, and RTL/failsafe behavior. Target-centering was validated in SITL but was not completed as a full real-world sequence before the competition ended. Physical validation also included an 8 kg structural load test, a 12-minute unloaded hover, a 7-minute hover with a 1 kg payload, and troubleshooting severe oscillation through PID gain adjustment.

projects.title: 6-DOF Cycloidal Robot Arm
projects.tagline: Custom 6-DOF cycloidal-drive robot arm; mechanical design complete, with prototyping, reducer validation, FEA, and ROS 2 integration in progress.
projects.timeline: Mechanical design completed Sep 2026 · Prototyping & ROS 2 in progress
projects.summary: An original 6-DOF desktop robotic-arm design built around five custom 27:1 cycloidal-reducer joints integrated into the structural links. The completed mechanical-design phase covers kinematic architecture, joint torque and inertia calculations, motor sizing, bearing and shaft selection, fits and tolerances, reducer packaging, DFMA, BOM development, manufacturing drawings, and a synchronized parallel gripper. Physical prototyping and ROS 2/URDF validation are the next stages.
features: 6-DOF anthropomorphic cobot-style topology with five custom 27:1 cycloidal-reducer joints
Joint torque and inertia calculations used for actuator sizing and mechanical architecture decisions
Bearing and shaft selection with dual-bearing supports to isolate structural loads from reducer and motor shafts
Fits, tolerances, reducer packaging, DFMA, BOM development, and manufacturing drawings prepared for fabrication
Synchronized parallel gripper and end-effector interface designed as part of the complete mechanical system
CAD structured for upcoming URDF generation, ROS 2 simulation, FEA, and physical reducer validation
projects.architecture: The arm uses a modular bridge architecture where each link carries the current joint reducer and supports the following joint motor. Five joints use custom 27:1 cycloidal reducers, while the wrist-roll axis is direct-drive. Bearings and shafts are selected to separate structural bending loads from the transmission, and the full SolidWorks assembly is organized for manufacturing documentation and later URDF/ROS 2 integration.
projects.results: The mechanical-design phase was completed in September 2026 with the full SolidWorks assembly, joint architecture, reducer geometry, torque/inertia calculations, actuator selection, fits and tolerances, BOM, and manufacturing drawings defined. The design targets a 450 mm reach and 0.60 kg payload. These remain design targets until fabrication and physical validation are completed.
contribution: Owned the complete mechanical-design phase: architecture definition, cycloidal reducer layout, joint calculations, actuator sizing, and packaging.
Selected bearings, shafts, fits/tolerances, and developed the BOM and manufacturing drawings for future prototyping.
Defined the next phase as reducer validation, FEA refinement, fabrication, and ROS 2/URDF integration.
